name: Zone 2 · tropical cacao guild
notes:
The Tropical Spa Guild: a cacao-led tree family that uses the sauna's warmth and the mister's humidity to push a micro-tropical pocket (Bright Tree is about 26.7° S, so cacao is marginal: protect it).
Canopy (existing): the mature Ice Cream Bean gives 40–70% dappled shade, nitrogen and leaf litter. Don't plant more: it is on the weed watch-list, so pick up pods and pull seedlings.
Mid layer: 1–2 cacao behind the stone walls in the lowest, dampest pockets, each on a slight mound over a hügelkultur base of punky Blackbutt scraps; coffee on the slightly higher, drier edge (pick cherries clean so birds don't spread it).
Climber: vanilla at the base of the mature trunks.
Herb carpet where the mister runoff collects: cardamom, gotu kola, Vietnamese mint, turmeric (galangal and ginger go to a sunnier hillside bed instead).
Planting: dust root balls with a commercial AM inoculant plus a trowel of soil from under healthy trees; cap beds with 10–15 cm coarse wood chip.
Feeding: sauna ash composted with Ice Cream Bean leaves first, never raw on the beds.
Cold: the pad slopes west and cold air drains west – don't dam it; fire the sauna on forecast frost nights (Jun–Aug).
Plant Sep–Nov; heavy work months March and September.
Source: Spa Guild handoff notes and PDC session 04 updates (Oct 2026).
